name: Plains
rule: Open plains and savanna. Travel is 3 miles per hour on foot, and a road through the terrain doubles that.

name: Hills
rule: Rolling or rugged hills. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour, or 2 miles per hour through the gentlest rolling country.

name: Forest
rule: Woodland. Light forest allows 2 miles per hour; dense, trackless forest slows travel to 1.5.

name: Desert
rule: Sand or scrub desert. Travel is 2 miles per hour, and foraging is difficulty 12 or worse.

name: Swamp
rule: Marsh and bog. Travel is 1 mile per hour; the ground is difficult and conceals ruins and hidden paths.

name: Mountains
rule: Mountain country and broken highland. Travel is 0.5 miles per hour; passes are few and defended.

name: Coast
rule: Shoreline and coastal water. A coastal road allows 3 miles per hour; a sailing ship makes about 6 miles per hour and can travel around the clock offshore.

name: Ruins
rule: Broken ancient ground. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour, and the rubble hides site entrances; exploring a site runs in 10-minute turns.

name: Tundra
rule: Cold, treeless ground. Travel is 2 miles per hour; exposure and scarce forage make long marches dangerous.

name: Glacier
rule: Crevasse-riven ice. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and a guide or ropes are needed to cross safely.

name: Volcano
rule: Ash slopes and lava country. Travel is 1 mile per hour; eruptions, poisonous air, and fires make the ground perilous.

name: Jungle
rule: Dense tropical forest. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and the canopy hides trails, ruins, and ambushes.

name: Moor
rule: Open heath and peat bog. Travel is 2 miles per hour; mist and soft ground make navigation hard.

name: Steppe
rule: Wide grassy plain. Travel is 3 miles per hour on foot, or 4 on horseback, with little cover.

name: Badlands
rule: Eroded gullies and broken rock. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; the country is easy to get lost in.

name: Farmland
rule: Tilled fields and hedgerows. Travel is 3 miles per hour; farm tracks count as roads for local journeys.

name: Ocean
rule: Open sea. A sailing ship makes about 6 miles per hour and can travel around the clock; small boats stay near shore.

name: Reef
rule: Shallow coral water. A boat must be poled or rowed at 2 miles per hour; larger ships cannot cross.

name: Island
rule: An isolated shore and its hinterland. Travel is 2 miles per hour; leaving needs a boat or a ford.

name: Plateau
rule: Raised tableland with steep sides. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; climbing to or from the rim costs extra time.

name: River
rule: Flowing water. Cross at a ford or bridge; travel along the bank is 3 miles per hour on foot.

name: Meadow
rule: Flower meadow and soft grass. Travel is 3 miles per hour on foot.

name: Pinewood
rule: Dark conifer forest. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; the canopy hides landmarks.

name: Canyon
rule: Sheer walls and a broken floor. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and the way down must be found.

name: Salt Flat
rule: Cracked white pan. Travel is 3 miles per hour when dry; there is no water or cover.

name: Ashland
rule: Cold ash and cinders. Travel is 2 miles per hour, and the air stings the throat.

name: Lagoon
rule: Calm, shallow water. A rowed boat makes 2 miles per hour, and the shallows can be waded.

name: Orchard
rule: Rows of fruit trees and mown grass. Travel is 2 miles per hour between the trunks.

name: Highland
rule: Wind-scoured upland. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; the weather turns quickly.

name: Bog
rule: Deep, sucking bog. Travel is 1 mile per hour, and the ground must be tested ahead.
